acceptance_gate: Blind joint truth tables, matched shared and rewired tasks including distractors; two primitive sharing controls and an equally informed inline entry.
completion_gate: Check minimum local width and physical separation, execute both returned outputs on all inputs and report the charged warm/cold comparison.
objective: From only paired Boolean truth tables, synthesize two outputs joined to an inferred minimal one- or two-bit intermediate. Compare paid verified cost with a strong primitive solver that can share arbitrary work and wires.
status: All 24 shared and 24 rewired rules returned minimum one- and two-bit programs. Supplied fold used 106.795 ms versus 99.823 ms primitive CPU including verification. The paid efficiency claim missed its gate; independent replay passed all 3,640 programs.
stop_rule: Use the prespecified total-cost and correctness conditions on the mixed stream; no scaling or learned selection on a miss.
title: Can two output tables reveal a shared hidden bit more cheaply with a fold?
